newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Albania pulls the plug on Western TV broadcasts.
newsitem.headline: Albania pulls the plug on Western TV broadcasts.

text.p: Albania on Monday pulled the plug on Western television broadcasts out of the country after declaring an immediate state of emergency to combat armed unrest in the south, the European Broadcasting Union said.

Tony Naetes, head of Eurovision News Services in Geneva, told Reuters that the EBU, the only agency providing satellite television feeds to the outside world from the capital Tirana, halted its work as of 1730 GMT after ordered to do so verbally by the Albanian authorities.

Naetes said the EBU's feed point in Tirana serving some 25 Western companies and channels including Reuters Television, the British Broadcasting Corporation, CNN, German networks ARD and ZDF, Italian RAI and French TFI had been shut down on 1730 GMT.

He said the EBU was the only agency providing Western satellite television feed out of Albania from its transmit earth station in Tirana. The EBU had not received any orders to leave the country and was seeking clarification, he added.

"We've just been told our licence is effectively suspended as a measure of the state of emergency," Naetes told Reuters. "There was no written confirmation, it was just a verbal order from a PTT representative. This effectively prevents the most visible way of reporting the conditions in the country."

Albania introduced a state of emergency and nationwide curfew on Monday as parliament elected President Sali Berisha to a second five-year term in office. It was not clear how the new official restrictions on the media apply to foreign news organisations.
